root_cause.text: The command stream parsing loop in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate` increments the index `i` for 64-bit commands but does not re-validate the loop bound before writing the second word, allowing an out-of-bounds write when `i` reaches `size/4`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "does not re-check the loop bound before writing the second word" and describes the scenario where `i == size/4 - 1` and bit 14 is set, causing `bocmds[size/4]` to be written past the allocation. The fix adds a bounds check `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` after incrementing `i`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The loop in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate` (lines 553-587) increments `i` for 64-bit commands without rechecking that `i < size/4` before writing to `bocmds[i]`. Specifically, when `i` reaches `size/4 - 1` and a 64-bit command is processed, `i` becomes `size/4` after the inner `i++` and the subsequent write `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]` is out-of-bounds. There is no bound check to prevent this, so the vulnerability is present and unfixed.
